## Proof

**Claim:** Yes. The space $C([0,1],[0,1])$ is dense in $\Pi_{[0,1]}[0,1]=[0,1]^{[0,1]}$ equipped with the topology of pointwise convergence (i.e., the product topology).

**Setup.** The topology of pointwise convergence on $[0,1]^{[0,1]}$ is the product topology, where each factor $[0,1]$ carries its usual topology. A basic open neighborhood of a function $f\colon[0,1]\to[0,1]$ has the form
$$
\mathcal{U}(f;\,x_1,\dots,x_n;\,U_1,\dots,U_n)
=\Big\{\,g\colon[0,1]\to[0,1]\;:\;g(x_i)\in U_i\text{ for }i=1,\dots,n\,\Big\},
$$
where $x_1,\dots,x_n\in[0,1]$ are finitely many points and each $U_i\subseteq[0,1]$ is an open neighborhood of $f(x_i)$. Only finitely many coordinates are restricted; all other coordinates are free.

**Density check.** We must show that every such basic open set contains a continuous function. Let $\mathcal{U}(f;x_1,\dots,x_n;U_1,\dots,U_n)$ be given. Reorder so that $x_1<x_2<\cdots<x_n$. For each $i$ pick a value $y_i\in U_i\cap[0,1]$ (possible since $U_i$ is an open neighborhood of $f(x_i)\in[0,1]$).

Define $g\colon[0,1]\to[0,1]$ by piecewise-linear interpolation through the points $(x_i,y_i)$:
- $g(t)=y_1$ for $t\in[0,x_1]$,
- $g(t)=y_i+\dfrac{t-x_i}{x_{i+1}-x_i}(y_{i+1}-y_i)$ for $t\in[x_i,x_{i+1}]$, $i=1,\dots,n-1$,
- $g(t)=y_n$ for $t\in[x_n,1]$.

(If $n=1$, only the constant pieces are used.) This $g$ is continuous on $[0,1]$. Since every $y_i\in[0,1]$ and linear interpolation between two values in $[0,1]$ remains in $[0,1]$, we have $g([0,1])\subseteq[0,1]$, so $g\in C([0,1],[0,1])$. Moreover $g(x_i)=y_i\in U_i$ for every $i$, hence
$$
g\in\mathcal{U}(f;\,x_1,\dots,x_n;\,U_1,\dots,U_n)\cap C([0,1],[0,1]).
$$

**Conclusion.** Every basic open set in the product topology intersects $C([0,1],[0,1])$ nontrivially. Therefore $C([0,1],[0,1])$ is dense in $\Pi_{[0,1]}[0,1]$ with respect to pointwise convergence. $\blacksquare$

### PROOF COMPLETE
